name: Editor Settings
description: Trim down WP's block editor — strip marketplace surfaces (Block Directory, remote patterns, Openverse, Font Library), tighten editor defaults, and drop the bits of block output we don't use (wp-elements-* classes, the core-block-supports inline stylesheet).

sections.title: Marketplace surfaces
sections.description: Removes the wp.org / wp.com / third-party content surfaces baked into the editor.

sections.title: Editor behaviour
sections.description: Tweak how the editor sets defaults for new content.

sections.title: Frontend output
sections.description: Strip block output we don't use before it reaches the wire.

settings.label: Disable the Block Directory
settings.description: Stops the editor from loading the wp.org marketplace assets (search-and-install third-party blocks panel). Equivalent to removing `wp_enqueue_editor_block_directory_assets`.

settings.label: Disable remote block patterns
settings.description: Stops the editor from fetching the wp.com pattern directory. Filters `should_load_remote_block_patterns` to false.

settings.label: Disable the Openverse media tab
settings.description: Hides the Openverse category in the media inserter. Sets `enableOpenverseMediaCategory` to false on editor settings.

settings.label: Disable the Font Library
settings.description: Hides the Font Library UI from Site Editor → Styles. Sets `fontLibraryEnabled` to false on editor settings. Theme-defined fonts in theme.json are unaffected.

settings.label: Force full-size images on posts
settings.description: Makes the editor default to inserting images at their full uploaded size on the built-in `post` post type. Doesn't apply to pages or custom post types.

settings.label: Strip core's default theme.json presets
settings.description: Wipes WP's built-in color palette / gradients / duotone / shadow presets, default font sizes, default aspect ratios, and the default spacing scale (set to 0 steps) on the `wp_theme_json_data_default` filter. The editor then only shows what the theme declares explicitly in its own theme.json. Recommended for Orbital sites where the theme owns the design tokens end-to-end.

settings.label: Strip wp-elements-* classes
settings.description: Removes the `wp-elements-{hash}` classes WordPress adds to blocks that use the Elements API for per-instance styling. Frontend only — leaves the editor alone so React's reconciliation keeps stable class lists.

settings.label: Drop the core-block-supports inline stylesheet
settings.description: Dequeues the `core-block-supports` stylesheet on the frontend — the inline CSS WP builds from block supports (typography, spacing, etc.). Only flip this on for themes that already cover supports in theme.json or their own CSS.

settings.label: Disable core layout styles
settings.description: Stops WordPress emitting the `.is-layout-flow` / `.is-layout-constrained` / `.is-layout-flex` / `.is-layout-grid` base CSS (margins, max-width centering, block-gap, alignment rules) into the global stylesheet, via core's `disable-layout-styles` theme support. The layout classes still land on block markup — the theme owns the CSS that styles them. Only turn on for themes that handle their own layout.
